ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A flow cytometer can count cells separately according to differences in the DNA content in the cells. Researchers treated cancer cells cultured in vitro with a certain anticancer drug, and after 24 hours used a flow cytometer to detect them; the results are as shown in the figure. Question: how many times the DNA content of the cells in peak b is that in peak a?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A flow cytometer can count cells separately according to differences in the DNA content in the cells. Researchers treated cancer cells cultured in vitro with a certain anticancer drug, and after 24 hours used a flow cytometer to detect them; the results are as shown in the figure. Question: how many times the DNA content of the cells in peak b is that in peak a?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there are two flow cytometry detection curve graphs of the control group and the experimental group; the horizontal axes are both “relative DNA content,” and the vertical axes are both “number of cells.” In the figure, peak a is located at about 40 on the horizontal axis, and peak b is located at about 80 on the horizontal axis. Then reason: the question asks how many times the DNA content of the cells in peak b is that in peak a; the horizontal coordinate corresponding to the peak can be used to represent the relative DNA content of this type of cell. Peak b is about 80, and peak a is about 40, therefore 80÷40=2. So the DNA content of the cells in peak b is 2 times that of peak a.
